title: Correcting Charges Posted in Error on a Respite and Short-Term Stay Statement
content:
A charge posted in error on a stay under the Respite and Short-Term Stay Agreement is corrected only by a billing-error credit referencing that exact charge entry, never exceeding it less earlier credits against it. Each charge entry receives at most one billing-error credit. A nightly charge that matches the stay type, nights and locked rate on record is not an error.

## The rule in parts

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| Means of correction | A billing-error credit, and only that |
| Object | The exact charge entry posted in error, which the credit references |
| Ceiling | The charge entry less any earlier credits against it |
| Frequency | At most one billing-error credit per charge entry, as the stay's ledger shows |
| Not an error | A nightly charge matching the stay type, nights and locked rate on record |

## Basis questions answered

**May one credit correct two charges posted in error?** No. Each billing-error credit references one exact charge entry.

**A charge of 500.00 has already received an early-departure credit of 200.00 and is found to be in error. What is the most a billing-error credit may be?** 500.00 less 200.00, that is 300.00 (hypothetical figures).

**A charge already carries a billing-error credit. May a second one be posted against it?** No; each charge entry receives at most one.

**A planned-stay segment bills the stay type, the planned nights and the locked nightly rate exactly as the stay record shows. Is it an error?** No; a nightly charge that matches the stay type, nights and locked rate on record is not an error.
